subject: MSA redline: special/consequential damages terminology - proposed compromise
body:
From: Sara Voss <sara.voss@horizon-legal.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Mark Lowe <mark.lowe@acme.com>
Date: Thu, Jul 30, 2026 at 09:12 AM -0700
Subject: MSA redline: special/consequential damages terminology - initial edits

Mina —

Attached is Acme's redline to the MSA (MSA_v3_Horizon_redline.pdf). Their procurement and GC teams pushed back on the one-way exclusion language we proposed. Key points from Acme: they want the exclusion to be mutual, and they propose to remove the term "special/punitive/incidental" in favor of a single definition of "Consequential Losses" tied to indirect/foreseeable losses. They'd also like to carve out confidentiality and IP infringement from the exclusion.

From Acme (high level):
- Mutual exclusion for consequential/special/incidental/punitive damages
- Carve-outs for confidentiality breaches and IP claims
- Cap remains as negotiated in order form (12 months of fees) but they want explicit language tying cap to "direct damages" only

They flagged the drafting around "willful misconduct" vs "gross negligence" — they prefer willful misconduct only as an exception, and they will not agree to a broad gross negligence carve-out.

See attached. Happy to jump on a call but wanted to surface this to your inbox first.

Thanks,
Sara Voss
Senior Counsel, Horizon Legal (on behalf of Acme)
Horizon Analytics

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, Jul 30, 2026 at 10:25 AM -07:00
Subject: Fwd: MSA redline: special/consequential damages terminology - initial edits

Ben / Laura —

Forwarding Acme's redline (attached). Please see the highlights below and advise on negotiation posture. I want to keep the conversation focused and minimize legal gymnastics during the commercial call Friday.

Summary of negotiation items I think matter operationally:
- Mutual vs one-way exclusion: Acme is pushing mutual; we currently have one-way in the draft (protects Redwood from consequential claims by customer).
- Definition wars: Acme proposes consolidating language into a single "Consequential Losses" definition. They want examples removed to avoid being boxed in.
- Exceptions: They insist on confidentiality and IP infringement carved out from the exclusion; they want willful misconduct (not gross negligence) as the exception.
- Cap tie: They want to say the cap applies to "direct damages only." We need to decide if we accept the cap language or push for broader protection.

Questions for Legal:
1) Operational risk if we switch to mutual exclusion and make the confidentiality/IP carve-outs — does that open material exposure for Redwood?
2) Is "willful misconduct" alone sufficient to cover proper exceptions? If not, can we accept that but adjust other clauses (indemnity, breach remedies)?
3) Any suggested phrasing that keeps the economic exposure limited while giving Acme something to sign?

Attachments: MSA_v3_Horizon_redline.pdf (original from Acme)

Mina Haddad
Senior Contracts Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, Jul 30, 2026 at 11:05 AM -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: MSA redline: special/consequential damages terminology - initial edits

Mina —

Agree we should avoid turning this into an all-or-nothing fight on terminology. Practical approach: give Acme a mutual exclusion but narrow the carve-outs and preserve cap mechanics that limit our exposure. Draft position below — feel free to iterate:

Proposed negotiation bullets (sales playbook):
- Offer: Mutual exclusion of consequential/special/incidental/punitive damages.
- Carve-outs (limited): (a) Losses arising from breach of confidentiality obligations; (b) IP infringement claims where Redwood's deliverables infringe a third party's IP; (c) payment obligations.
- Clarify that "Consequential Losses" do not include direct, reasonably foreseeable costs to mitigate/restore service.
- Replace "gross negligence" with explicitly defined "willful misconduct" and then add a short list of material harms that are uncapped for willful misconduct (e.g., deliberate data exfiltration).
- Cap: Maintain cap at the greater of USD 250,000 or 12 months of fees paid under the applicable Order Form.

Operational note: If we accept mutual, insist on explicit language limiting consequential to indirect/foreseeable — i.e., examples are ok if they protect us (lost profits, lost savings). Remove overly broad terms such as "any loss of business or goodwill."

If Legal says we can't accept the confidentiality carve-out (because of data risk), we push for: carve-out only for statutory data breach claims and regulatory fines, not for contractual incidental losses.

Ben Carter
Head, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, Jul 31, 2026 at 09:02 AM -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: MSA redline: special/consequential damages terminology - initial edits

Mina / Ben —

Legal's read: we can accept a mutual exclusion with narrow, enumerated exceptions, but we should be careful with any language that effectively removes the cap or converts consequential into "direct" by definition. Specific recommendations below: 

1) Definitions: keep a short definition for "Consequential Losses" that references indirect or unforeseeable harms and provide a short, non-exhaustive list (e.g., lost profits, loss of data use, loss of business). This helps the court-level interpretation and prevents Acme from expanding scope later.

2) Exceptions: accept carve-outs for: (i) breach of confidentiality (limited to demonstrable remediation and statutory obligations), (ii) IP infringement (limited to actual damages awarded in final judgment or settlement), and (iii) payment obligations. Do NOT accept a blanket carve-out for regulatory fines or exemplary/punitive damages.

3) Willful misconduct vs gross negligence: we should prefer "willful misconduct or gross negligence" as the standard that defeats the exclusion. If Acme insists on "willful misconduct" alone, we can accept that only if we broaden the enumeration of excluded harms (i.e., explicitly include intentional data exfiltration, deliberate tampering, and known security bypass). The reason: willful misconduct is a higher bar and harder to prove; without gross negligence we could end up defenseless for serious but reckless acts.

4) Cap mechanics: retain a monetary cap that is the greater of (i) $250,000 OR (ii) 12 months of fees. Add explicit language: "For the avoidance of doubt, the Cap applies to Direct Damages only and does not apply to liability for (a) breach of confidentiality to the extent statutory fines apply, (b) IP infringement adjudicated in final judgment, or (c) indemnified third-party claims." This preserves carve-outs where necessary.

5) Practical negotiation tactic: propose a mutual exclusion with the above carve-outs, but put in a short "escalation" paragraph — if Acme's GC will not accept gross negligence language, offer a session with Redwood's CSO to walk through security controls and to add a Service Level credit mechanism for certain outages.

I'll draft a counter-redline based on these points unless you want to convene a call.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Sara Voss <sara.voss@horizon-legal.com>, Mark Lowe <mark.lowe@acme.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, Aug 01, 2026 at 02:10 PM -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redline: special/consequential damages terminology - proposed compromise

Sara / Mark —

Thanks for the redline and for surfacing Acme's position. Redwood is prepared to move toward a compromise to keep things moving on the commercial timeline. Below is our counter-proposal (we will produce a redline):

Redwood counter (high level):
- Exclusion: Mutual exclusion for Consequential, Special, Incidental and Punitive Damages (defined succinctly as indirect or unforeseeable losses).
- Carve-outs (narrow): (a) Losses resulting from breach of confidentiality obligations (limited to documented remediation costs, statutory obligations, and direct costs reasonably incurred); (b) Third-party claims for IP infringement attributable to Redwood deliverables (limited to amounts awarded in final judgment or settlement); (c) Customer payment obligations.
- Standard: "Willful misconduct or gross negligence" defeats the exclusion. If Acme insists on only "willful misconduct," Redwood requests a short, enumerated list of behaviors (e.g., intentional data exfiltration) that will be uncapped.
- Cap: The Cap on liability will be the greater of USD 250,000 or 12 months' fees under the applicable Order Form, and for the avoidance of doubt the Cap applies to Direct Damages only. Carve-outs in the preceding paragraph are not subject to this Cap to the extent explicitly stated (IP judgments; statutory fines where applicable).

We are open to a short call to walk through the compromise. If Acme is willing to accept mutual exclusion with the limited carve-outs and the "willful misconduct or gross negligence" standard, we can finalize the MSA redline and proceed to the Order Form sign-off without further escalation.

Please find our proposed redline attached (MSA_v3_Redwood_counter_redline.pdf).

Best,

Mina Haddad
Senior Contracts Manager
